cells.tense: You're in the room when things end, and you can tell which endings are the necessary ones — nothing is being forced and nothing is being dragged out.
cells.ask: say the fair thing out loud before you've weighed it.
cells.core: What's arriving at your threshold arrives on time, and you're meeting it on time. You can feel when something has run its course, and you let it go without making a case for it and without pretending it could have gone on. That's rarer than it sounds, and it's what keeps the space clear enough for the next thing to come in.\n\nEquity is the next thing this balance is free to feed — fairness that moves through you without being tallied. Give and receive in the exchange that's already open: say what's right here, take what's offered, and let the leveling happen without a ledger. What arrives then is the plain sense that things are square, and you didn't have to earn it.
cells.sheetLine: You're letting what's finished finish, and you know it.
cells.verb: letting what's finished actually finish so the next thing can start

cells.tense: You're bracing for the next ending before this one has arrived, and the clearing has become a way of living rather than a moment in it.
cells.ask: stay with one person's difficulty for a day without solving or ending it.
cells.core: Endings are your reflex right now. Something starts and you're already looking for the exit, calling it honesty, calling it freedom — and the people around you are watching you leave things before they've had a chance to happen. The upheaval isn't transformation; it's the fear of being caught by something you can't control, dressed up as liberation.\n\nWhat's actually needed here is the opposite move: not another ending, but staying close enough to feel what someone else is carrying. Be near one person's difficulty for a day. Don't fix it, don't finish it for them, don't decide it's over. Just be in the room with it and let that be enough. What returns is the recognition that you're still there with them, and that the room hasn't collapsed.

cells.tense: You're standing at a door that's already behind you, holding on to something that has finished and waiting for it to come back.
cells.ask: let one thing end today, and notice what moves in you when it does.
cells.core: Something in your life has already run its course, and you're still there, tending it, calling it loyalty. The loyalty is real — that's what makes it hard — but it's loyalty to a shape that's gone, and the holding on is taking the place of the next thing that wants to arrive. You're not stuck because you can't move; you're stuck because moving means letting something die that you haven't given up yet.\n\nDrive is what's needed, and it doesn't come from pushing. It comes from feeling — from letting genuine engagement with what's actually here give you direction. Let one thing end today. Not all of it, not a grand declaration — one thing. And notice what starts moving in you once it does. What you get back is momentum that came from your own feeling, not from force.

cells.tense: Something in you is already ending, and you're talking about it as if nothing were changing — the pen is down, and the page is still moving.
cells.ask: name the one thing that's already over, out loud, once.
cells.core: You're not someone who avoids endings; you're someone who hasn't noticed this one yet. It's happening — you can feel the ground shifting under conversations, under plans, under the way you spend your days — but you're describing your life as if it were the same as last year. The transformation is running. The acknowledgment isn't.\n\nAuthority is what's needed here: not control, but the structure that lets you see what's actually in front of you. Name the one thing that's already over. Say it out loud, once, to yourself or to someone. You don't have to act on it, don't have to end anything formally — just stop calling it still open. What you get back is the clarity that comes from saying what's true, and the relief of not having to pretend anymore.
cells.sheetLine: Something's already ended. You're still calling it current.
